COMAPA Nuevo Laredo will shut down its North Plant on Friday, Nov. 27, from 9 a.m. to 9 p.m. to connect a new water line and improve drinking-water service in the city's northwest sector, the utility announced.

The work will connect a 30-inch by 8-inch water line at the intersection of Carretera Piedras Negras and Boulevard Colosio Norponiente. The 12-hour shutdown covers draining the line before the work begins and refilling it once the connection is complete, according to the utility.

COMAPA will use the same shutdown to review the electrical systems that power the North Plant, with support from the Federal Electricity Commission. Crews will inspect the wiring, the substation and the starters to prevent failures and keep pumping to the northwest sector running, the utility said.

During the shutdown, low pressure or no water is possible in the 17 colonias served by the North Plant: Reservas Territoriales, Fraccionamiento El Progreso, Naciones Unidas I and II, Los Artistas, Nueva Victoria, Olivos 1 and 2, Fraccionamiento Cumbres, Fraccionamiento San Roque, Arboledas, Guerreros del Sol, Bonitos Toboganes, Unión del Recuerdo, Bayito, Nuevo Bayito, Colorines and Praderas del Mezquital.

Service will return gradually once the work is finished, and the farthest neighborhoods and those on higher ground may take a few more hours to regain normal pressure, COMAPA said. The utility urges residents to store water before the shutdown begins, use water responsibly while the work is underway, and report any leaks or problems to 073.

Sources: La Voz de Tamaulipas, Nov. 24, 2026; El Chusco, Nov. 24, 2026.

title: COMAPA to Shut Down North Plant Friday, Nov. 27; Low Pressure or No Water in 17 Northwest Colonias
